requirement:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Given the following project structure:

 - Project A
    - `ProjectA.MyType`

 - Project B
    - References
        - Project A
    - Package References
        - MessagePack
    
I need to have a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for type `ProjectA.MyType` generated **inside Project B** instead of Project A, because the latter has no (and cannot have) reference to MessagePack nuget package.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that will work for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.

For example:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

That's it. The class does not even need to declare a body (no `{` and `}`), because the actual implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:

1 - Use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes. This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

2 - Allow the generator and analyzers to work with user-defined versions of the MessagePack attributes. This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`. With this, I could simply copy and paste the attribute definitions for MessagePack attributes such as `[Key]` into my Project A, and have the source-generated formatter (as described above) pick them.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly. This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency. Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.

## Motivation

Project A is really a library (Nuget package), and I really want to keep it minimal. It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

story.summary: Adds a public `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute with an optional `SurrogateType` property. The source generator now fills in the body of a user-declared `partial` class that implements `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`, even when `T` lives in an assembly with no MessagePack reference. It also registers that class in `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Without a surrogate, `T` is serialized contractless: public read-write members, string keys, sorted by name. With a surrogate, the `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` attributes on the surrogate define the contract, and its members are matched to `T`'s members by name and type. Four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019–022) reject bad declarations. The change also adds docs, a MessagePack-free test library, execution tests and generator diagnostic tests.
story.why: REQ-2129: Project B must be able to source-generate a formatter for `ProjectA.MyType`, where Project A cannot reference MessagePack. The surrogate is the agent's own design for keyed contracts. It is not one of the three options the issue lists.

story.confidence_overview: Plumbing looks consistent: attribute discovery, pipeline merge, partial-class emission and diagnostics. The contractless member collector has an off-by-one (`i < targets.Count - 1`) that drops the alphabetically last member. That should make the contractless execution tests fail (ExternalPerson.Label, ExternalPoint.Y, and the 0x82 map header). Surrogate mode does not go through that loop and looks correct. The diagnostic tests cover MsgPack019/020/021 (abstract only), 022 and 005. The parameterless-constructor check, generic data types and callback receivers are untested.

refusals.what: New public API in a shipped package
refusals.why: Public API is a promise to every user; once released it cannot be taken back without a breaking change. A human owner decides.
New diagnostics break builds that treat warnings as errors and become part of the package's contract.

refusals.what: New diagnostic descriptors and their message texts.
Contractless wire format for external types: a string-key map of public read-write members sorted by ordinal name. Surrogate string keys get sequential indices.
refusals.why: Defines the serialized output for these types going forward, and the current loop already drops a member.

findings.description: Off-by-one: `for (int i = 0; i < targets.Count - 1; i++)` drops the last member in ordinal name order, and a type with one member gets zero. ExternalPerson would serialize only Id (Label lost), and ExternalPoint only X. ContractlessClassRoundTrips, ContractlessClassUsesStringKeysForPublicReadWriteMembers (expects 0x82), ContractlessStructRoundTrips and MessagePackObjectCanContainExternalTypes should fail. If they pass, the generated code is not coming from this loop.

Surrogate mode iterates all instance fields and properties of the surrogate, including private, readonly and non-public members. Any such member without [Key] or [IgnoreMember] aborts generation with MsgPack004, so a surrogate with a private helper field cannot be used.

GeneratedFormatterRequest carries INamedTypeSymbol instances through the incremental pipeline. Symbols differ per compilation, so the record never compares equal and every edit re-runs collection and the diagnostics pipeline. This defeats incremental caching and can root old compilations.
NoDeserializingConstructor is created with no message arguments. If the existing descriptor's message format has placeholders, the message renders unformatted. This path is untested.
GeneratedFormatterRequest is declared public in the generator assembly, although only internal code uses it.

not_quoted: As for the attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), I can think of 3 alternatives:
This is too limited IMO, as it cannot have `Union` and other features.

This would be similar to how you can declare dummy versions of BCL attributes that the C# compiler expects, such as [`[IsExternalInit]`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/67687186/643085) or `[ModuleInitializer]`.

3 - Source-generate the attributes themselves using [`IncrementalGeneratorInitializationContext.RegisterPostInitializationOutput`](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/main/docs/features/incremental-generators.md#outputting-values) instead of them existing in the `MessagePack.Annotations` assembly.
This would allow using the attributes without adding an additional runtime dependency.
Only compile-time reference to the analyzer Nuget would be required.
It currently has zero dependencies and I would really like to keep it that way.

The source generator now fills in the body of a user-declared `partial` class that implements `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`, even when `T` lives in an assembly with no MessagePack reference. It also registers that class in `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Without a surrogate, `T` is serialized contractless: public read-write members, string keys, sorted by name. With a surrogate, the `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` attributes on the surrogate define the contract, and its members are matched to `T`'s members by name and type. Four new error diagnostics (MsgPack019–022) reject bad declarations. The change also adds docs, a MessagePack-free test library, execution tests and generator diagnostic tests.","why":"REQ-2129: Project B must be able to source-generate a formatter for `ProjectA.MyType`, where Project A cannot reference MessagePack.
